findings.reason: the §7 selection path cannot run without naming the JT-60SA shot-range/physical-identity source and extending gs/machine_identity.py's default_registry/identity_for_shot to be machine-parameterised, so the plan must state that owner rather than leave it to the open jt60sa-artifact-authoring question (which covers authoring, not identity resolution).
findings.text: §7 has ArtifactMachineSelector.select (gs/machine_selection.py:135) resolve a shot through identity_for_shot (gs/machine_identity.py:207), whose default_registry is nova's MAST geometry registry MachineGeometryRegistry and whose select() raises when the shot lies outside the MAST registry's shot ranges; the plan proposes the selector "takes the machine from the catalogue the shot belongs to and passes it to the identity registry, the pin table and the plan (which forbids a JT-60SA module in nova, §1) never names where JT-60SA shot ranges and its physical identity are held, so §7 either forks the identity owner or is unimplementable for E101173/integer JT-60SA shots

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — each new module is a single-entry point hiding substantial behaviour (selene_deck.py one converter entry point over the deck grammar + geo.in + vessel block; eddb_remote.py one batch fetch + one cache writer; the EQDB reader one remote script charging the §3 transport), and the store-addressing change extends NetCDFTransformEngine (transform_engine.py:236) rather than spawning a store engine per format.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §7 routes JT-60SA shot selection through a machine-identity mechanism whose current owner cannot answer for a JT-60SA shot, and the plan does not name the owner to extend.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — supplied counts public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; each section that adds surface states what it retires or why nothing can (the §2 exporter, §3 extractor and §4 converter retire nothing because ambix has no exporter/remote reader/deck reader today; the §4 probe-angle slot retires the machine branch; the §4 two store-addressing slots retire nothing because the catalogue had no addressing slot and they move read_geometry_table's MAST defaults into the catalogue; §7's two record fields retire nothing).
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan cites ~15 existing mechanisms by file path (paths.py MIRROR_ROOT/JT60SA_ROOT, description_reader.py read_geometry_table, transform_engine.py NetCDFTransformEngine.open, artifact_resolution.py PINNED_* constants, cocos_convention.py, challenge/convention.py, eval/efit_referee.py, spine_bench/transform_geometry_source.py, machine_map.py map_for_loader), and every load-bearing citation I opened is accurate.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — every wrapper carries its "why not extend" in its own text: the §3 extractor over codex's remote layer (importing it would drag the graph/LLM/tool-installer into every read), the tokamap exporter kept out of the loaders, the receipted netCDF over a deck store engine (no per-shot cost to amortise), and the EQDB reader reusing the §3 transport/cache.
